neet_phy_u10_t01_1.working: e^{-ωt} decays monotonically and never repeats, so it is non-periodic. The other three are sums or powers of sinusoids, which are periodic.

neet_phy_u10_t01_3.working: sin²(πt) = (1 − cos 2πt)/2. Angular frequency is 2π, so the period is 2π/2π = 1 s.

neet_phy_u10_t01_4.working: A: √2 sin(ωt + π/4) is SHM with period 2π/ω (II). B: (1 − cos 2ωt)/2 is SHM about mean 1/2 with period π/ω (III). C is periodic but not SHM (IV). D is non-periodic (I).

neet_phy_u10_t01_5.working: A is true: cos²ωt = (1 + cos 2ωt)/2, period π/ω. B is false: a sum of two different frequencies is not SHM. C is true. D is false: log ωt is not periodic. E is true by Fourier's theorem. So A, C and E.
